subject: POC workshop: prompt inventory rehearsal, guardrails & evening load-test window
messages:
From: Kate Lin <kate@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt workshop & load-test

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team at Acme is keen to move straight into a hands-on session where we can:
- do a prompt inventory walkthrough (identify our 25 high-priority prompts)
- validate structured output / guardrails for our billing reconciliation flows
- exercise routing behavior (fallbacks to smaller models)
- run a short load-test window to see latency/cost numbers under realistic concurrency

We attached an updated POC scope and a pre-filled PromptInventory_Template.csv to this thread.

Availability: our preferred slots next week (PST):
• Tue 12/1, 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00
• Thu 12/3, 18:00–20:00 (we can do an evening slot for the load test)

Questions for planning:
1) Can Redwood run a 30-minute load test at ~50 concurrent sessions?
2) Do you need sanitized data or will synthetic prompts be sufficient?

If you can confirm a proposed schedule and the lead contacts, we’ll send calendar invites and pre-reads.

Thanks,
Kate Lin
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Analytics

Attachment: POC_Scope_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: PromptInventory_Template.csv (csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Lin <kate@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — hands-on prompt workshop & load-test

Hi Kate —

Appreciate the clear ask and the pre-filled template — that’s perfect. Quick answers up front:
- Yes, we can run a 30-minute load test at ~50 concurrent sessions in a dedicated evening window.
- Synthetic prompts are fine for the initial load run; if you want results on production data we’ll need a short data handling checklist (privacy/KMS note).

Proposed plan:
1) Workshop (2 hours) — prompt inventory, structured-output tests, guardrail configs, routing rules
2) Follow immediately (same evening, if you prefer) with a 30-minute ramped load test

Proposed slots from our side:
• Tue 12/1, 14:00–16:00 PT — workshop + optional later load-test (we can push load-test to 18:00)
• Thu 12/3, 18:00–20:00 PT — workshop + load-test in the final 30 minutes (recommended)

Ben — can you confirm we have two GPUs reserved in Dedicated for a 50-concurrency ramp at the Thu evening window?
Lauren — can you prepare the structured-output test harness (JSON schema validation + guardrail examples)?

If Thursday 12/3 evening works for you, we’ll send one invite for 18:00–20:00 with a follow-on load-test block.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.ai

Vivek / team —

Confirming resource plan: I’ve reserved two Dedicated GPU instances for Thu 12/3 from 17:30–20:30 PT to allow for a warm-up period and the 30-minute load window at ~50 concurrent sessions. We’ll stage the ramp as: 10, 25, 40, 50 across 5-minute increments, then a 10-minute steady-state sample.

A couple quick asks to make the session efficient:
- Kate/Tom: please flag the top 10 prompts you want validated for structured output and any golden responses you care about. If possible paste them into the PromptInventory_Template.csv under the "critical" column.
- Vivek/Lauren: I’ll own the load harness and will instrument token-level latency. Lauren — I’ll need the JSON schema examples by Wed EOD so I can wire up the validators.

I’ll draft an invite once Kate confirms the preferred slot.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks all — Thu 12/3, 18:00–20:00 PT works best for us. We’ll plan for the workshop to run 18:00–19:30 and the load-test 19:30–20:00.

Action items from Acme:
- I uploaded a filled PromptInventory_Template.csv (critical prompts marked) to the Drive folder linked above.
- We will use synthetic, anonymized prompts for the load test.
- Tom will be the primary POC for the session (looping him on the invite).

Requests for Redwood before the session:
1) Please add a short pre-read (1 page) outlining the guardrail toggles we’ll exercise.
2) Include Zoom link, the Drive folder, and a short runbook in the calendar invite.

If you want, we can make the invite recurring for a weekly follow-up during the POC (optional).

Thanks — looking forward to Thursday.

Best,
Kate Lin
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Analytics
